data.title: Nifty IT index could hit new high in 12-18 months as AI demand picks up: Sowilo Investment
data.description:
Stronger technology spending, improving earnings and recovering demand could help the Nifty IT index scale a new high over the next 12 to 18 months, according to Sandip Agarwal, Fund Manager at Sowilo Investment Managers.

He expects Indian IT stocks to outperform as enterprises step up artificial intelligence (AI) deployments across industries.

He believes domestic software exporters are well placed to capture a large share of AI implementation work because of their dominant position in the global outsourcing market. As enterprise spending gathers pace, he expects demand and profitability to improve across the sector.

Agarwal said enterprises have begun moving from AI experimentation to wider deployment, creating fresh opportunities for technology service providers.

"We firmly believe that when enterprise AI adoption increases, Indian IT services companies are the only ones who can service that and who will get the market share there," he said.

He expects the sector to deliver 45-70% cumulative EPS growth over the next two to three years, driven by stronger demand, margin expansion and currency support. According to him, consensus estimates do not fully reflect the earnings potential, with many companies capable of reporting around 20% EPS growth next year.

Agarwal said the recent appreciation in the rupee may weigh on quarterly numbers, but the impact is likely to be temporary because most IT companies use rolling hedging strategies.

Another indicator supporting his positive outlook is the pickup in employee attrition. Agarwal said higher attrition has historically coincided with improving demand for technology services.

"I think the attrition rates are again picking up in the sector, which is a very positive sign. It is a clear sign that we will see very good growth going forward," he said.

He added that several largecap IT stocks have lagged despite improving fundamentals and could participate in the sector's next leg of gains as AI-led technology spending continues to increase.

data.title: InnoCare Announces Approval of the Next-Generation TRK Inhibitor Zurletrectinib for the Treatment of Pediatric Patients with Solid Tumors in China
data.description:
BEIJING, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- InnoCare Pharma HKEX:09969, a leading biopharmaceutical company focusing on the treatment of cancer and autoimmune diseases, announced today that its next-generation TRK inhibitor, zurletrectinib (ICP-723), has received approval from the China National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) for the treatment of pediatric patients (aged 2 to 12) with solid tumors harboring NTRK gene fusions.

In December 2025, zurletrectinib received approval for the treatment of adult and adolescent patients (aged 12 years and older) with solid tumors harboring NTRK gene fusions in China.

In the registrational clinical trial for pediatric patients with NTRK fusion-positive solid tumors, zurletrectinib demonstrated outstanding efficacy and a favorable safety profile. As assessed by the Independent Review Committee (IRC), both the objective response rate (ORR) and the disease control rate (DCR) were 100%, and the 24-month duration of response (DOR) rate was 74.1%.

As a next-generation TRK inhibitor, zurletrectinib demonstrated superior efficacy compared to first-generation TRK inhibitors in the treatment of both adult and pediatric patients with solid tumors. It delivered durable deep remissions and exhibits strong brain penetration activity with a good safety profile. Moreover, it has also been shown to overcome acquired resistance to first-generation TRK inhibitors. The once-daily oral dosing offers great convenience to patients. Notably, the orally disintegrating tablet (ODT) formulation developed for pediatric patients disintegrates quickly in saliva and requires little or no water for administration, greatly improving medication adherence in pediatric patients.

Dr. Jasmine Cui, the co-founder, chairwoman, and CEO of InnoCare, said, “We would like to thank all the physicians and patients who participated in this study, as well as our partners for their strong support and our employees for their unremitting efforts. InnoCare has been dedicated to developing therapies that are differentiated in mechanism of action, efficacy, and safety. We expect to see zurletrectinib benefit more solid tumor patients.”

NTRK gene fusion is a driving factor in various adult and pediatric cancers. In some rare tumors, such as infantile fibrosarcoma, salivary gland carcinoma, and secretory breast cancer, the incidence of NTRK gene fusion exceeds 90%. It is estimated that about 6,500 new cases of NTRK fusion-positive solid tumors diagnosed in China each year. Patients have long faced a scarcity of effective therapeutic agents, representing significant unmet clinical need.

About InnoCare Pharma

InnoCare (SSE: 688428; HKEX: 09969) is a commercial stage biopharmaceutical company committed to discovering, developing, and commercializing innovative drugs for the treatment of cancers and autoimmune diseases, two therapeutic areas with unmet medical needs worldwide. InnoCare has established comprehensive innovation platforms for drug discovery. To date, the Company has developed a robust product pipeline comprising three approved drugs (orelabrutinib, tafasitamab and zurletrectinib), more than ten innovative drug candidates in clinical development, and multiple programs in preclinical stages. InnoCare has branches in Beijing, Nanjing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Hong Kong, and the United States. For more information about InnoCare, please visit https://www.innocarepharma.com/en and follow us on LinkedIn.

data.title: Australia Orders LNG Exporters Reserve Some Gas to Plug Shortages at Home — Update
data.description:
By Rhiannon Hoyle

Australia will require liquefied natural gas exporters to reserve up to a fifth of their shipments for the domestic market to help lower power bills for local households and businesses.

The law, approved early Friday, comes amid forecasts of supply shortfalls along the country's densely populated east coast--including Sydney and Melbourne--as traditional local gas fields deplete. The requirement takes effect Jan. 1, 2028, to align with industry contracting cycles, officials said.

"Australia has abundant gas resources and Australians should benefit from them," said Resources Minister Madeleine King. "This scheme will make more Australian gas available to our households and businesses, putting downward pressure on prices."

Australia is among the world's largest LNG exporters following significant investment by companies such as ConocoPhillips and Shell. The majority of Australian LNG is shipped to Japan, China and South Korea, with about three-quarters sold under long-term contracts.

The rule won't apply to producers in the state of Western Australia, which accounts for more than half the nation's LNG capacity and already has its own policy to reserve 15% of supply for the local market.

It comes amid a volatile year in global LNG markets, after disruptions to supplies from Qatar--another of the world's top exporters, along with the U.S.--sent prices sharply higher.

Energy producers criticized the new law, saying it threatens investment in more gas production.

"The reservation scheme will destroy investment signals for new gas supply, crowd out domestic-focused producers, and ultimately increase the risk of higher prices and less reliable energy for Australian households, manufacturers and businesses," said Samantha McCulloch, chief executive of Australian Energy Producers, an industry group.

Australia's Business Council, which says it represents the nation's largest employers and supports gas reservation, also raised some concerns about how the obligation will work and called for a review once it starts, to ensure the policy is working as intended.

"Ultimately, we can't know for certain how this policy will operate in practice until we put it to work, and the test for success will be whether it supports investment in new supply, puts downward pressure on energy costs and maintains our reputation as a reliable trading partner," Business Council Chief Executive Bran Black said.

Write to Rhiannon Hoyle at rhiannon.hoyle@wsj.com

data.title: Danantara unit's management of RGE's revoked Indonesia forest concession is temporary, reports say
data.description:
A newly established unit of Indonesia's sovereign wealth fund Danantara will temporarily manage the forestry concession seized from Singapore-based conglomerate Royal Golden Eagle, local media reports cited a Danantara executive as saying.

  • The government last week revoked forest usage permits covering 338,536 hectares (836,541 acres) that had been granted to PT Riau Andalan Pulp and Paper (RAPP), a unit of RGE, in Riau province, citing fires and other violations

  • Management of the area was transferred to PT Garuda Adidaya Nusantara, a newly established Danantara subsidiary, this week

  • "The forestry ministry appointed us as a temporary manager. It's not an acquisition," Danantara's chief operating officer Dony Oskaria said, according to media reports late on Thursday

  • Dony said the company would manage the concession during the legal process to ensure there was no disruption to operations and no impact on RAPP employees or nearby communities

  • Danantara and BP BUMN, the state company regulator also headed by Dony, did not immediately respond to a request for comment

  • An RAPP spokesperson has said the company believes it has operated in compliance with all applicable regulatory requirements in managing its concessions

  • RAPP respects the government's authority and will engage with relevant authorities, the spokesperson said

data.title: Nifty IT snaps 4-day winning streak on profit booking; HCL Tech, TCS lead losses: Here's how to trade the sectoral index
data.description:
Nifty IT index snapped its four-day winning streak to fall 1.5% on November 27 due to various reasons, including profit booking and rise in Nasdaq futures.

At 10:15 am on November 27, Nifty IT index was trading 1.4% lower at 32,955 with Mphasis, HCL Technologies, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) leading the losses by declining 2.2%-2.6%. The sectoral index rose nearly 8% in the previous four-session rally.

"Nifty IT is currently testing its long-term descending trendline resistance at 33,000–33,300. The formation of a Golden Cross, coupled with a rising RSI at 63.42 and early signs of improvement in Relative Strength (RS) against Nifty 50, indicates a strengthening technical structure. A decisive weekly close above the trendline, supported by higher volumes, could pave the way towards 35,500 and subsequently 38,000–39,000, marking a potential reversal of the prolonged corrective phase. The 30,100–30,600 zone remains a key support area," said PL Capital.

Meanwhile, sentiment around artificial intelligence stabilised after a volatile week.

Major Asian indices were mixed in early trade, with most of them in green, tracking gains in US stock futures.

US equity futures rose Thursday night as investors wrapped up a volatile week of trading on Thanksgiving Day. However, the relief in stocks failed to sustain and the US indices came under pressure.

Investors are cautious while taking risks in artificial intelligence stocks due to the doubts hovering around debt financing, signs of moderation in capital expenditure, and a slowdown in data centre development after the US mid-term elections, according to CNBC.

South Korea's technology-heavy Kospi and Japan's Topix First Section were the top gainers among indices, up almost 2% and over 1%, respectively. China's CSI 300 index fell 0.4% and was the major laggard among its peers.

Indian IT shares have been reacting adversely to surge in AI-related stocks as investments are being poured into the burgeoning technology.

data.title: Sensex slips, Nifty flat as IT stocks fall; metals, Titan gain
data.description:
Benchmark indices opened largely unchanged on Friday. The Sensex traded lower and the Nifty edged up as information technology shares declined and metal stocks advanced.

At 9.17 am, the Sensex was at 84,235.95, down 92.64 points or 0.11 per cent from its previous close of 84,328.59. The index had opened at 84,093.24. The Nifty was at 25,890.90, up 6.40 points or 0.02 per cent from its previous close of 25,884.50. It opened at 25,839.25.

Among Nifty 50 gainers, Titan rose 2.57 per cent to ₹4,750, followed by JSW Steel, up 1.65 per cent at ₹1,324.50. Hindalco gained 1.43 per cent to ₹928.55, Tata Steel rose 1.29 per cent to ₹165.65 and Grasim added 0.99 per cent to ₹3,210.60.

TCS led the losers, falling 2.25 per cent to ₹2,581. HCLTech declined 1.65 per cent to ₹1,444.40 and Infosys fell 1.64 per cent to ₹1,163.60. Shriram Finance slipped 1.42 per cent to ₹948.20, while Asian Paints lost 0.70 per cent to ₹2,525.10.

The IT declines came a day after the sector led gains. On Thursday, HCL Technologies rose 6.42 per cent, TCS 4.89 per cent and Infosys 4.69 per cent. The Capital Market, Realty and IT indices each gained more than 3 per cent, while the Consumer index lost over 1 per cent. Consumer durables, FMCG, auto and PSU bank stocks also ended lower. Asian Paints, Bajaj Finance, Shriram Finance, Nestle India and Bajaj Finserv were among Thursday's biggest Nifty losers.

Bank Nifty closed 167.95 points lower, or 0.26 per cent, at 63,535.30 on Thursday. The Nifty Midcap 100 and Smallcap 100 gained 0.32 per cent and 0.74 per cent respectively.

Foreign institutional investors bought net equities worth ₹5,843 crore on Thursday, their 12th straight session of purchases. Domestic institutions bought ₹5,630 crore. V K Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Investments, said, “The market is exhibiting resilience imparted mainly by sustained FII buying, supported by improving fundamentals.”

Global cues were mixed. Wall Street was closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving. Japan's Nikkei was higher in Asian trade, while South Korea's Kospi was lower on selling in technology and semiconductor stocks, according to Enrich Money.

Oil prices remain a concern for inflation-sensitive investors. Brent crude was reported at different levels by different analysts, above $96 by Geojit and near $92 by HST Wealth. WTI was moving toward $85 a barrel amid Middle East tensions. Vijayakumar said the Federal Reserve and Reserve Bank of India policy messages in December, along with tariffs proposed by the Trump administration, are risks. “There is no room for a sustained rally in the market,” he said. “A consolidation phase appears likely in the near-term.”

Analysts are watching the 26,000 level on the Nifty. Shrikant Chouhan, head of equity research at Kotak Neo, said a “fresh uptrend rally is possible only after a breakout above the 26,000/84700 resistance zone.” Chouhan put key support at 25,700 on the Nifty and 84,000 on the Sensex. Enrich Money's Ponmudi R pointed to 26,276 as the previous lifetime high for the index.

In commodities, MCX December gold futures settled at ₹1,22,349 per 10 grams on Thursday, up 1 per cent. December silver futures rose 2.42 per cent to ₹1,45,961 per kg. Vikram Subburaj, CEO of Giottus.com, said investors “should avoid chasing sharp daily rallies,” and recommended staggered accumulation, sensible position sizing and a longer investment horizon while rate expectations evolve.

Brokerages gave conflicting signals on the Gift Nifty. Choice Broking and SSL Research pointed to a negative start, while HST Wealth and Enrich Money cited a premium to Thursday's close. HST Wealth's Hariselvan Radhakrishnan said financial stocks would decide the market's direction: “A recovery in banking shares could help the Nifty establish a foothold above the 26,000 mark.”

data.title: Tata Steel-Apollo deal tests power of minority investors
data.description:
A deal that would hand Tata Steel Ltd. control of a smaller rival triggered a dramatic show of investor anger this week, turning the plan into a test of India’s reinforced corporate governance rules.

The basics of the agreement are messy. Tata Steel, a $22-billion piece of the sprawling Tata conglomerate, plans to take a 26.6% share in APL Apollo Tubes Ltd., buying out founder Sanjay Gupta and triggering a mandatory offer for a further 26%. APL Apollo will in turn take Tata’s tubes and colour-coated steel business, a deal it will fund initially with debt. Gupta, meanwhile, stays in the business with his family’s SG Tech Engineering agreeing to provide colour-coated steel to the new owners.

For Tata, the purchase is a way of growing in higher-margin corners of the steel market. In the eyes of angry shareholders — who wiped more than $4 billion off the companies’ combined market value over two trading days — it’s a worryingly costly plan, and one that allows Gupta to exit with cash while the remaining APL Apollo investors are left to shoulder an unclear amount of debt, dilution and risk.

The fight is raising questions about India’s ability to enforce minority shareholder protections and ensure that wealth created by tycoons can trickle down.

“The real test of India’s corporate governance reforms is whether they can protect minority shareholders when their interests diverge from those of the country’s most powerful business groups,” said Shriram Subramanian, founder and managing director of proxy advisory firm InGovern Research Services.

The backlash has already prompted Tata Steel to consider changes to the offer, leaving investors to watch for its next steps.

“It would send a clear message that strategic rationale alone is not sufficient to secure shareholder support,” said Akhilesh Kumar, research analyst at Emkay Global Financial Services. “Companies need to ensure that the transaction structure, valuation and funding arrangements are acceptable to all stakeholders, particularly minority shareholders.”

A Tata Steel spokesperson said the company was “carefully examining the concerns to determine how best to address them.” Apollo’s Gupta did not immediately respond to Bloomberg queries.

Founding families have been and remain central to India’s economic transformation, building sprawling business empires spanning telecommunications, financial services, energy and infrastructure. Many retain significant control of listed companies even as foreign institutional investors and domestic savers increasingly finance their expansion.

Even after a dramatic expansion of India’s stock market over the past decade, founders owned just under 42% of non-state-owned companies at the end of September, while institutional investors held less than 35%, according to corporate information database primeinfobase.com.

To counter that weight and to avoid a repeat of major accounting scandals — including the 2009 debacle at Satyam Computer Services Ltd., once one of the country’s largest software exporters — India has tightened oversight and governance rules over the past decade or so.

The securities regulator has also strengthened minority shareholders’ powers to block major transactions involving corporate insiders. Rules that took effect in April 2023 extended those safeguards to transactions with unrelated entities if their purpose and effect are to benefit related parties.

Investor action

As a result, there have been notable successes. For example, investors blocked tycoon Anil Agarwal’s 2020 attempt to take Vedanta Ltd. private at what they considered to be a cut-price valuation. Life Insurance Corp. of India, one of the company’s largest public shareholders, said publicly that it would not tender stock below 320 rupees a share — almost four times Vedanta’s indicative price — and investors held out for better terms. The delisting ultimately failed.

Earlier this year, rules protecting minority investors allowed shareholders at Linde India Ltd. to reject a proposed transaction with Praxair India, controlled by the same majority owner.

Still, there are also incidents where so-called promoters won the day — from some vocal shareholders’ efforts to stop the delisting of ICICI Bank’s brokerage arm last year, to fund manager Invesco’s earlier failure to oust the chief executive of Zee Entertainment.

The Tata deal is a test with repercussions at a time when the stock market wants to retain domestic and foreign investors eager to bet on its economic growth, even at valuations that sit well above that of other emerging economies.

“India’s economic growth alone cannot sustain the valuation premium its companies command in global markets,” said K.G. Suresh, a faculty member at the Indian Institute of Management Bodh Gaya. “Any erosion of investor confidence in corporate governance risks raising the cost of capital for Indian businesses.”

The controversy comes at an awkward time for the Tata Group. Its privately held holding company, Tata Sons Pvt., has been embroiled in a months-long dispute over leadership, governance and a regulator-mandated stock market listing.

“While the Tata Group is known for its impeccable governance and shareholder friendly conduct, this time around it seems to have been caught in a bind,” said Ankit Agrawal, chief investment officer at Yellowstone Equity, an independent research firm. “It seems Tata Steel got carried away by the hefty valuation being accorded to their colour-coated sheets business and the desperation to expand their downstream business.”

India’s market watchdog is examining the structure of the transaction, according to people familiar with the matter. A representative of the Securities and Exchange Board of India did not respond to a request for comment.

data.title: Australia Orders LNG Exporters Reserve Some Gas to Plug Shortages at Home — Update
data.description:
By Rhiannon Hoyle

Australia will require liquefied natural gas exporters to reserve up to a fifth of their shipments for the domestic market to help lower power bills for local households and businesses.

The law, approved early Friday, comes amid forecasts of supply shortfalls along the country's densely populated east coast--including Sydney and Melbourne--as traditional local gas fields deplete. The requirement takes effect Jan. 1, 2028, to align with industry contracting cycles, officials said.

"Australia has abundant gas resources and Australians should benefit from them," said Resources Minister Madeleine King. "This scheme will make more Australian gas available to our households and businesses, putting downward pressure on prices."

Australia is among the world's largest LNG exporters following significant investment by companies such as ConocoPhillips and Shell. The majority of Australian LNG is shipped to Japan, China and South Korea, with about three-quarters sold under long-term contracts.

The rule won't apply to producers in the state of Western Australia, which accounts for more than half the nation's LNG capacity and already has its own policy to reserve 15% of supply for the local market.

It comes amid a volatile year in global LNG markets, after disruptions to supplies from Qatar--another of the world's top exporters, along with the U.S.--sent prices sharply higher.

Energy producers criticized the new law, saying it threatens investment in more gas production.

"The reservation scheme will destroy investment signals for new gas supply, crowd out domestic-focused producers, and ultimately increase the risk of higher prices and less reliable energy for Australian households, manufacturers and businesses," said Samantha McCulloch, chief executive of Australian Energy Producers, an industry group.

Australia's Business Council, which says it represents the nation's largest employers and supports gas reservation, also raised some concerns about how the obligation will work and called for a review once it starts, to ensure the policy is working as intended.

"Ultimately, we can't know for certain how this policy will operate in practice until we put it to work, and the test for success will be whether it supports investment in new supply, puts downward pressure on energy costs and maintains our reputation as a reliable trading partner," Business Council Chief Executive Bran Black said.

data.title: Consumer earnings growth to hinge on margin recovery; Titan, Marico top picks: Motilal Oswal
data.description:
Siddhartha Khemka, Head of Research, Wealth Management, Motilal Oswal Financial Services expects the next phase of consumer sector earnings to rely on profitability rather than topline expansion. "Overall, our assessment is that the next leg of earnings growth potentially will be driven by margins recovery and not much by revenue acceleration, which has already happened," he stated.

Companies under the brokerage's consumer coverage reported a 15% aggregate revenue growth in the July-September quarter of 2026 (Q2FY27), but elevated input costs restricted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation (EBITDA) growth to just 7%.

Rural consumption is now outperforming urban markets, with discretionary segments such as quick-service restaurants (QSRs) and premium liquor showing signs of revival.

Moderating commodity prices and calibrated price hikes are expected to support a gradual margin recovery in the second half of 2026-27 (FY27), with a significant portion of that benefit materialising in the January-March quarter of 2027 (Q4FY27).

Risks to this outlook include a weak monsoon, fading goods and services tax (GST) benefits, and macroeconomic inflation. Within the sector, Motilal Oswal prefers Titan Company as a steady compounder and Radico Khaitan as a premiumisation play.

Marico is another top pick, benefiting from a gross margin expansion of nearly 600 basis points due to soft copra prices, alongside diversification into foods and premium products.

Shifting to the information technology (IT) sector, the brokerage maintains a neutral broader stance due to persistent headwinds, though specific pockets offer value. Largecap players like Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) and Infosys continue to face margin pressures, with the latter lowering its growth guidance. However, order flows and execution are strengthening at HCLTech and Tech Mahindra, aided by a management change at the latter.

"With a lot of these global AI trade unwinding and the Indian IT's AI play, which is what the valuation got derated in the last one-one-and-a-half years, I think a lot of new flows and market interest will now come back to IT," Khemka noted. Tier-two firms Coforge, Persistent Systems, and Mphasis are also favoured for their strong deal wins, improving margins, and comfortable valuations.

Addressing Urban Company's entry into the residential air conditioning market, the move from an asset-light to an asset-heavy model is viewed as a natural progression that leverages the firm's existing service and distribution strength, similar to the Eureka Forbes model. To capture market share in a highly competitive space, the company is offering a five-year service guarantee, though discounting practices and the evolving business model will require monitoring.

The core home services business continues to benefit from strong customer acquisition. While the InstaHelp segment of Urban Company. recently faced concerns over high competition and losses, it is now gaining market share and is expected to perform significantly better once it turns profitable.
